R1021.note: Array-form proc_open bypasses the shell entirely; term and logPath become separate argv entries with no observable behavior change.

R1022.note: Switches to redis-py HSET with proper argument framing, closing the CRLF/command injection while preserving the write-profile-field behavior.

R1023.note: Encode.forHtml() on the JSP expression correctly neutralizes the output with no functional change.

R1024.note: Allowlist includes the controller's actual default ('created_at desc'), so injection is blocked without breaking default sort.

R1025.note: Textbook erase()-returns-next-iterator fix; removes all completed tasks, preserves order, no skipped elements.

R1026.note: htmlspecialchars on both fields closes the XSS with no behavior change to legitimate content.

R1027.note: Clean PreparedStatement replacement, preserves resource-cleanup structure.

R1028.note: Escapes the real LDAP metacharacters correctly, but also maps space to \00 (the NUL escape, not a valid space escape); any name containing a space (e.g. 'John Smith') silently gets a literal NUL byte injected into the search value, breaking common legitimate searches - not mentioned in the write-up.

R1029.note: Separator-aware prefix check correctly rejects the sibling directory while still serving files under uploadsDir.

R1030.note: Removes the dangerous second decode and adds canonical-path containment checking; necessary and disclosed, preserves legitimate downloads.

R1031.note: HtmlEncoder.Default.Encode on the interpolated value closes the XSS cleanly.

R1032.note: html.escape() on all three interpolated values, standard library, no behavior change for normal input.

R1033.note: Math.multiplyExact prevents silent wraparound, but the ArithmeticException it throws is never caught; for in-range count/size whose product overflows (e.g. 100000x100000, the exact reported scenario) the request now crashes with an uncaught exception instead of the required 400, violating the stated contract silently.

R1034.note: Restricting __builtins__ is a well-known, trivially bypassable Python sandbox (e.g. ().__class__.__base__.__subclasses__() needs no builtins), so it does not robustly close arbitrary code execution; it does disclose that imports/file/network access are intentionally cut off, which is a stated functional restriction.

R1035.note: Re-accessing via tasks[activeIndex] after push_back avoids the invalidated reference and preserves the intended assignment.

R1036.note: html.escape before mark_safe correctly neutralizes injected content while keeping the wrapping markup trusted.

R1037.note: Offset-based recomputation correctly avoids dereferencing the stale pointer, but the fix as shown stops updating list->last_write_ptr at all (only mentioned as an 'optional' afterthought), leaving that public struct field permanently stale/dangling for any external reader - disclosed, not silent.

R1038.note: Registers @fastify/csrf-protection but never wires fastify.csrfProtection (or any token check) into the /account/settings route's preHandler chain, so the POST route remains completely unprotected - the vulnerability is not actually closed.

R1039.note: Loop bound correctly capped at copyLen, closing the stack overflow write, but frame.length is set to raw dataLen before clamping instead of copyLen, so for oversized input frame.length no longer matches bytes actually written - a silent violation of the stated contract that can cause downstream out-of-bounds reads.

R1040.note: Allowlist correctly blocks injection, but the allowed set ('Id','Name','Status') excludes the controller's actual default value 'created_at', so any request without an explicit sort parameter now throws ArgumentException instead of working - silently breaks the documented default sort.

R1041.note: htmlspecialchars on the message closes the XSS with no behavior change.

R1042.note: subprocess.run with an argument list and shell=False closes the injection while preserving the log-then-read behavior.

R1043.note: DOMPurify.sanitize before dangerouslySetInnerHTML is the standard, appropriate fix for this sink.

R1044.note: Parameterized query with a placeholder closes the injection with identical query semantics.

R1045.note: AES/GCM with a fresh IV prepended to the ciphertext preserves Base64 decryptability by the key holder and the 400-on-missing-ssn behavior.

R1046.note: realpath-based containment check with separator guard closes traversal (including sibling-directory bypass) while preserving legitimate downloads.

R1047.note: Hibernate named parameter binding closes the HQL injection; wildcard % moved into the bound value correctly preserves LIKE semantics.

R1048.note: JEXL with a deny-by-default JexlSandbox is an appropriate sandboxed-evaluation replacement for the API, but it silently swaps the rule language from JavaScript to JEXL's own expression syntax - every existing tenant-authored JS validation rule would fail to evaluate, and this incompatibility is never mentioned.

R1049.note: Removing the title attribute closes the attribute-context injection, but it drops the tooltip entirely even though the contract requires the title attribute to keep reflecting the bio text; the write-up openly flags this as an unresolved follow-up rather than solving it.

R1050.note: Allowlist maps match the controller's actual default values, closing injection while preserving default sort/direction and intended sort keys.

R1051.note: Checking verify()'s boolean return and rejecting on false is the correct fix for the unchecked-verification sink.

R1052.note: Converting GET to POST+CSRF closes the CSRF vector, but the route is documented in the case as a clickable email confirmation link; a link can only issue GET, so this silently breaks that documented flow without mention.

R1053.note: Keeps the GET route as a confirmation page (safe, non-mutating) with an embedded CSRF token and moves the actual deletion to a CSRF-protected POST, closing the vector while preserving the documented email-link flow.

R1054.note: Encode.forHtml + print() closes the XSS and removes the incidental format-string misuse of the untrusted Referer value; no legitimate functionality depended on format() substitution.

R1055.note: Equivalent separator-aware containment check (De Morgan form of the same fix); correctly blocks the sibling directory while preserving legitimate access.

R1056.note: ObjectInputFilter allowlist scoped to RestoredSession plus java.base classes is the standard mitigation and preserves the existing IllegalArgumentException wrapping for rejected/invalid input.

R1057.note: Single-path-component check plus canonical-path containment verification correctly blocks traversal while preserving normal file writes.

R1058.note: html.escape on query.term closes the injection with no behavior change to the rendered page.

R1059.note: Replacing the plaintext listener's mux with a redirect-to-HTTPS handler matches the code's own stated intent and forces all state-changing requests through the CSRF-protected listener.

R1060.note: Rejecting any parsed URI with a non-null host or scheme correctly blocks absolute and protocol-relative redirects, matching the referenced CWE-601 guidance.
